previous_statement: An extended D_*t-isomorphism is in particular the extended D_*t-inclusion required by lem-maincb-reset-invariant-preservation. Substitute D=D_* there: D_*>=1; W.c0_cb=c0>=max{c0^0,K_floor,C_unit(K_floor+1)}; W.r_reset is at most epsilon_max^cb, delta_max^cb/D_*, e_it/(D_*+1), epsilon_unit, delta_unit/max{1,K_floor}, a_unit/((1+K_disp)D_*), and [2(1+K_disp)D_*]^{-1}; and each call has 0<=t<=W.r_reset, epsilon_R<=t, map defect at most D_*t, and unit error at most D_*t. These are precisely that lemma's hypotheses, so each literal call is reset-eligible and meets the stated M02/M03 and near-unit thresholds.
new_statement: For the global-scalar and Stage-1 calls, nodes 1.3 and 1.4 explicitly provide the extended D_*t-inclusion hypothesis; with D=D_*, D_*>=1, W.c0_cb=c0>=max{c0^0,K_floor,C_unit*(K_floor+1)}, the displayed W.r_reset bounds, 0<=t<=W.r_reset, epsilon_R<=t, and unit error <=D_*t, lem-maincb-reset-invariant-preservation applies to those two calls. For the Stage-2 and Stage-3 calls, however, nodes 1.5 and 1.6 provide only extended D_*t-isomorphisms. Under the exact registered definitions and allowed external inputs there is no premise establishing that either map is an extended D_*t-inclusion; a recorded raw-defect bound is not such a premise by def-maincb-raw-call. Therefore reset eligibility for u_2 and u_3, and hence the parent assertion for all four calls, is not established in this workspace without registering def-extended-delta-inclusion or adding an allowed bridge lemma.
